cases.name: Neha v. State (Neha Bora)
cases.topic: Security for keeping peace – Ss. 126, 130, 135 BNSS
cases.tag: Writ court will not test an Executive Magistrate's subjective satisfaction behind a peace-bond notice; but all material must be disclosed and an interim bond under S. 135 needs a real apprehension of breach.

cases.name: Bipin Satish Chandra Agrwal v. State of Maharashtra
cases.tag: Arrest for an offence under three years without S. 41-A CrPC compliance and mechanical remand without reasons is illegal; State to pay Rs 5 lakh, act against the officers and refer the magistrate's role.

cases.name: P.A. Inamdar v. State of Maharashtra
cases.topic: Death by negligence – S. 304A IPC (S. 106 BNS)
cases.tag: College teachers are not criminally liable under S. 304A IPC for adult students drowning at a public beach on a picnic: no proximate rashness, and the event was beyond their control. FIR quashed.

cases.name: Yuvajana Sramika Rythu Congress Party v. State of Andhra Pradesh
cases.tag: Interim order: courts normally keep out of an ongoing election, but may step in when muscle power or illegal means block free nominations; the SEC under Art. 243ZA must ensure candidates can file unhindered.

cases.name: Pinarayi Vijayan v. K.M. Shajahan
cases.topic: FIR ordered by court – standing of accused; S. 175(4) BNSS
cases.tag: Interim order: persons named in an FIR that a court ordered can appeal that order; the Court noted S. 175(4) BNSS, unlike S. 156(3) CrPC, requires a superior's report and the public servant's version first.

cases.name: Bharat Kumar v. State of Bihar
cases.tag: Codeine cough syrup within the Centre's permitted concentration limits is a matter for the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, not the NDPS Act; the Court faulted police for routinely booking such seizures under NDPS.

cases.name: Dr. M.K. Ravi Varma v. National Institute of Technology
cases.topic: Service law – recovery of excess pay
cases.tag: Teachers who signed undertakings had to repay wrongly granted pay; the Court noted that no-recovery precedents never considered S. 72 of the Contract Act and Article 142 rulings are not binding.

cases.name: Suo Motu Civil Reference v. Union of India
cases.bench: Sathish Ninan, P. Krishna Kumar JJ
cases.tag: Section 69 of the Indian Succession Act, under which a Christian's will is revoked by marriage, is constitutionally valid; it has a legitimate aim and is not discriminatory because Hindus are excluded.

cases.name: Ayishath Ruksana v. State of Kerala
cases.bench: Anil K. Narendran, Muralee Krishna S. JJ
cases.tag: Detention order and grounds must be served in a language the detenu understands; serving a Kannada speaker otherwise breaches Article 22(5), so the KAAP Act detention was set aside.

cases.name: Biju v. State of Kerala
cases.tag: An appellate court cannot enhance a sentence on its own motion, but it may order a retrial where the trial court wrongly acquitted on a charge despite credible victim testimony.

cases.name: S v. J
cases.tag: A father's remarriage and a child from the new marriage are not grounds to reduce maintenance payable to a child of the first marriage.

cases.name: Mohammad Haroon v. Union of India
cases.tag: Black-marketing should ordinarily be handled under the PBMSEC Act; using the NSA to detain for a year where that Act caps detention at six months is a perversion of the law.

cases.name: H v. H
cases.tag: Persistently pressuring an only son to abandon his elderly widowed mother and live separately amounts to mental cruelty, entitling him to divorce under Section 13 HMA.

cases.name: M/s I Think Apps Pvt. Ltd. v. Anugya Gupta
cases.tag: An objection to subject-matter jurisdiction under Order VII Rules 10–11 CPC must be decided before an amendment application; a court lacking jurisdiction cannot allow an amendment to cure it.

cases.name: Danish v. State of U.P.
cases.bench: Ujjal Bhuyan, Atul S. Chandurkar JJ
cases.tag: Separate trial is the rule under S. 218 CrPC (now BNSS); two incidents close in time with the same accused are not one transaction when the places and victims differ, so a joint trial was set aside.

cases.name: Indroneel Goho v. Razouvonuo Thong
cases.tag: An arbitration clause does not by itself bar a criminal case, but cheating (S. 420 IPC / S. 318 BNS) needs dishonest intent at the start; a later breach of an MoU is a civil dispute, so the complaint was quashed.

cases.name: Najeeb v. State of Kerala
cases.tag: A conviction for selling obscene CDs cannot rest only on the investigating officer's word; the trial court must itself view the material before deciding it is obscene.

cases.name: Preeti Sharma v. State of Madhya Pradesh
cases.tag: Access to electricity is part of the right to life under Article 21, so an occupier is entitled to a connection even while ownership of the property is in dispute.

cases.name: Ramnath Mishra v. Special Police Establishment
cases.tag: The sanctioning authority must apply its own mind to the evidence before allowing prosecution of a public servant, and cannot simply follow the Special Judge's prima facie findings.

cases.name: Devinder Singh v. Union Territory of J&K
cases.court: Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh High Court
cases.tag: Caste abuse of a woman who is not herself a Scheduled Caste member does not attract the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act merely because her husband is; bail granted.

cases.name: UT of J&K v. Neeru Pandita
cases.court: Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh High Court
cases.tag: Under S. 5 of the J&K Civil Services (Special Provisions) Act, 2010 the right to regularisation accrues when the statutory conditions are met, not on the date of the formal order; the 150-day limit is procedural.

cases.name: Saradindu Chakravarty v. Union of India
cases.tag: The National Commission for Scheduled Castes only advises and recommends; it has no power to adjudicate and so cannot declare an FIR to be false.

cases.name: Perivemula Venkateswarlu v. Mediga Anjaiah
cases.tag: A temporary injunction must record reasons on prima facie case, balance of convenience and irreparable loss; status quo cannot be ordered without first finding who was in possession before the suit.

cases.name: Yarragorla Itukanalu v. State of Andhra Pradesh
cases.tag: Where police refuse to register an FIR, the complainant should first go to the SP and then the Magistrate under S. 175(3) BNSS before seeking a writ under Art. 226, unless real urgency exists.

cases.name: Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Purama Raghavamma
cases.topic: Motor accident claims / transfer of policy
cases.tag: An insurer cannot escape paying accident compensation merely because the policy was not transferred to the vehicle's new owner, if the policy was in force on the accident date (S. 157 MV Act).

cases.name: A. Amaranadh Babu v. Marreddy Anjaneya Reddy
cases.tag: A S. 138 NI Act notice is valid if, read as a whole, it clearly demands the cheque amount; it need not repeat the figure in its closing paragraph.

cases.name: Mohammad Yusuf Mohammad Punjani v. Gujarat State Waqf Board
cases.tag: The State Waqf Tribunal's powers are adjudicatory only; it cannot exercise supervisory control over how the Waqf Board manages a waqf.

cases.name: United India Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Chandrakant Vishandas Harwani
cases.bench: N.S. Sanjay Gowda, J.L. Odedra JJ
cases.tag: An owner of goods travelling with them in a goods vehicle is not a gratuitous passenger, so the insurer must pay for his injuries; compensation was also enhanced.

cases.name: L v. B
cases.tag: A Scheduled Tribe couple who admit marrying by Hindu rites can seek mutual-consent divorce under the HMA; the Family Court could not demand proof of dissolution under tribal custom.

cases.name: Kashif Khan v. High Court of Judicature for Rajasthan
cases.bench: Sanjay K. Agrawal CJ, Baljinder Singh Sandhu J
cases.tag: Posts left vacant by non-joining or later resignation are fresh vacancies to be filled by new recruitment; wait-listed candidates have no automatic right to them.

cases.name: Vikram Singh v. State of Rajasthan
cases.tag: Release on probation lifts the disqualification under S. 12 Probation of Offenders Act; non-disclosure of that conviction does not automatically justify dismissal without weighing the circumstances.

cases.name: Monu Mohammed v. State of Rajasthan
cases.tag: Whether private defence was exceeded is judged from the accused's position facing imminent danger, not by calm hindsight or by counting injuries in isolation.

cases.name: Tejaram v. State of Rajasthan
cases.tag: Prior approval under Section 17A PC Act is not needed to probe a bribe demand, since demanding a bribe is a criminal act unconnected with any decision or recommendation made in official duty.

cases.name: Rajkumar Madki v. Dr. Shailendra Beldal
cases.tag: A private complaint for filing a false election affidavit under Section 125-A RP Act is maintainable and is not subject to the Section 195 CrPC bar on complaints by courts.

cases.name: Satinder Pal Singh v. Bedi Hospital
cases.bench: Pamidighantam Sri Narasimha, Alok Aradhe JJ
cases.tag: Until a binding contract is concluded, a public authority may recall or revisit an auction to secure a better price; fresh e-auction directed.

cases.name: K. Ramalingam v. Government of Tamil Nadu
cases.bench: Pamidighantam Sri Narasimha, Alok Aradhe JJ
cases.tag: Inam land dedicated to a deity cannot be gifted, even to the State; such a gift is void from inception and no sanction under the TN HR&CE Act can cure it. The State, as trustee, cannot take it for itself.

cases.name: Rano Singh v. Gurbax Singh
cases.bench: Aravind Kumar, Vipul M. Pancholi JJ
cases.tag: A bare suit for possession fails where a registered sale deed clouds the plaintiff's title; declaratory relief must be sought. An agreement to sell creates no interest in property.

cases.name: Senior Intelligence Officer v. Mohammed Kamran
cases.tag: An accused may challenge arrest and seek bail at the same time, but pursuing both while hiding one from the court is an abuse of process.

cases.name: R. Saravanan v. Periyar University
cases.bench: Prashant Kumar Mishra, Shree Chandrashekhar JJ
cases.tag: A Letters Patent bench should not upset a just decision of the writ court merely because it spots some error or prefers another view; Single Judge's order restored.

cases.name: S. Gururaj v. Additional Chief Secretary
cases.tag: Reclassifying land as mixed-residential in a zoning plan does not wipe out the State's rights over a water body; demolition of flats built on it was upheld once an alternative site had been allotted.

cases.name: Mahesh Chandra Joshi v. State of Rajasthan
cases.tag: Serious allegations alone cannot justify indefinite custody; once the probe is done, evidence is documentary and trial is far off, continued detention becomes punishment without trial and breaches Art. 21.

cases.name: YES Bank Ltd. v. Axis Trustee Services Ltd.
cases.bench: Dipankar Datta, Augustine George Masih JJ
cases.tag: An Administrator appointed for a bank under the Banking Regulation Act cannot exercise RBI's regulatory power to write down AT-1 bonds; such power cannot be implied from a general savings clause.

cases.name: Just Rights for Children Alliance v. S. Harish
cases.bench: J.B. Pardiwala, K. Vinod Chandran JJ
cases.tag: Internet access is a fundamental right under Arts 19(1)(a) and 21 that children also hold; Court refused a blanket social-media ban and laid down measures on CSEAM removal, digital safety and sex education.

cases.name: M.S. Sharma Enterprises v. National Building Construction Corporation
cases.bench: Aravind Kumar, Vipul M. Pancholi JJ
cases.tag: A contractual bar on interest worded to cover interest 'or otherwise' is absolute; an arbitral tribunal bound by the contract cannot award pre-reference or pendente lite interest against it.

cases.name: Deepak Raheja v. Omkara Assets Reconstruction Pvt. Ltd.
cases.bench: Dipankar Datta, Augustine George Masih JJ
cases.tag: Default under Section 7 IBC need only be shown on a preponderance of probabilities; the NCLT need not reconcile accounts forensically. Court also deprecated citing AI-generated, non-existent judgments.

cases.name: Sunil Kumar v. IFFCO Tokio General Insurance Co. Ltd.
cases.tag: A victim who has lost all earning capacity and needs a lifelong attendant may be treated as 100% functionally disabled even if the medical disability percentage is lower; compensation more than doubled.

cases.name: Madhu Kudapa v. Lodha Healthy Constructions & Developer Pvt. Ltd.
cases.bench: Pamidighantam Sri Narasimha, Alok Aradhe JJ
cases.tag: A homebuyer refunded with interest for the builder's delay cannot also recover rent for the same period, as that would be double compensation.

cases.name: Secretary to the Government of Tamil Nadu v. Sameer Ahmed
cases.bench: Prashant Kumar Mishra, Shree Chandrashekhar JJ
cases.tag: Conversion does not by itself make a person a member of a backward-class Muslim community, and pre-conversion caste status does not carry over; Madras HC's quashing of the Government Order upheld.

cases.name: Mahammed Hanif v. State of Karnataka
cases.tag: Posters calling a Supreme Court verdict a 'denial of justice' are protected dissent; S. 153A is judged by the effect on reasonable people at large, not on a few. FIR quashed.

cases.name: Commissioner of Central Tax v. Sreenivasa Rao Ravinuthala
cases.tag: Limitation for a s.62 IBC appeal runs from pronouncement of the NCLAT order; only time to get a certified copy is excluded

cases.name: Sanjay Sureka v. Directorate of Enforcement
cases.bench: Aravind Kumar, Vipul M. Pancholi JJ
cases.tag: Though Section 19 PMLA fixes no number of days, the arrest order and material must be forwarded to the Adjudicating Authority immediately; bail was granted to the accused.

cases.name: Dr. B.C. Roy Engineering College v. State of West Bengal
cases.bench: Pamidighantam Sri Narasimha, Alok Aradhe JJ
cases.tag: The full fee for a professional course must be notified before admission; mid-course hikes are allowed only in exceptional cases, and fee committees' decisions are open to High Court review.

cases.name: Dhanlaxmi Merchandise Pvt. Ltd. v. State of Madhya Pradesh
cases.bench: Aravind Kumar, Vipul M. Pancholi JJ
cases.tag: Rejecting the highest bid as inadequate needs material on present market value; comparing it with the bidder's own earlier bid is not enough. Cancellation of sand-mining auctions set aside.

cases.name: Alladin Charities and Zakat Wakf v. Mohammed Saleem
cases.tag: When obstruction to a possession decree raises title questions under Order XXI Rule 97 CPC, the executing court must decide them after a full inquiry under Rule 101; matter remanded.

cases.name: Sanjay Prasad v. Madhusudan Dwivedi
cases.tag: Referred to a larger bench whether writ jurisdiction under Article 226 can be labelled civil or criminal, a question that decides whether an intra-court (Letters Patent) appeal is barred.

cases.name: District Court Bar Association v. State of Kerala
cases.bench: Soumen Sen CJ, Syam Kumar V.M. J
cases.tag: The State must appoint Special Public Prosecutors who handle only POCSO cases within six weeks, instead of loading them with other juvenile justice work.

cases.name: Abhishek Upadhyay v. State of Uttar Pradesh
cases.bench: Surya Kant CJI, Joymalya Bagchi J
cases.topic: Police demand for personal digital data
cases.tag: Police cannot seek a person's private digital data for the period before the alleged offence; after an FIR such data may be sought only if other ways of tracing the accused fail. Notice to X quashed.

cases.name: Agri S.S. Krishnamurthy v. Speaker, Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly
cases.tag: Speaker may accept an MLA's resignation during disqualification proceedings but must still decide them

cases.name: State of Maharashtra v. Sudhir s/o Motiramji Hiwarkar
cases.tag: Where relief would fasten financial liability on the public exchequer, the State itself must be impleaded; joining only an officer or department leaves the writ petition fundamentally defective.

cases.name: Kusumlal Sao v. State of Chhattisgarh
cases.tag: Murder and evidence-tampering convictions set aside: the chain of circumstances was broken and, given the deceased's history of substance abuse, the defence theory of an accident was a probable one.

cases.name: Shaji v. State of Kerala
cases.tag: Placing the penis on a child's genitals is not mere touch under S. 7 POCSO but penetrative assault under S. 3; under S. 42 only the higher POCSO sentence applies, not a separate S. 376AB IPC term.

cases.name: ARCIS Clean Energy Pvt. Ltd. v. Parshva Innovation
cases.tag: A named venue does not automatically become the seat of arbitration; the juridical seat is found by reading the arbitration agreement as a whole.

cases.name: Haramani Sahoo v. Lalita Nayak
cases.tag: An Order VI Rule 17 CPC amendment should not be refused at the threshold on limitation when limitation is arguable and turns on disputed facts, such as when the plaintiff learnt of a document.

cases.name: Chavan Dharmendar v. State of Telangana
cases.bench: J.B. Pardiwala, K. Vinod Chandran JJ
cases.tag: A bank's alleged breach of RBI guidelines in dealing with a borrower does not become an SC/ST Act offence merely because the borrower's directors are SC/ST; absent caste-based insult, the FIR was quashed.

cases.name: Hardev Construction Pvt. Ltd. v. Union of India
cases.bench: J.B. Pardiwala, K. Vinod Chandran JJ
cases.tag: A tendering authority cannot reject a bid for not meeting a tender condition that was plainly impossible to comply with; the Patna HC order upholding the rejection was set aside.

cases.name: Renuka Jain v. State of NCT of Delhi
cases.bench: Ujjal Bhuyan, Atul S. Chandurkar JJ
cases.tag: A victim has standing to ask the High Court under s.528 BNSS to expedite the trial

cases.name: Sultan Singh (Dead) through LRs v. Financial Commissioner, GNCTD
cases.tag: A Hindu widow's limited interest became absolute under s.14(1) HSA; succession follows the law in force at her death

cases.name: Chittibarika Chandra Shekar v. State of Telangana
cases.bench: JB Pardiwala, K Vinod Chandran JJ
cases.tag: Refusing to marry, even if suicide follows, is not by itself abetment of suicide

cases.name: Martanda Singh v. State of Chhattisgarh
cases.bench: JB Pardiwala, K Vinod Chandran JJ
cases.tag: A three-year consensual relationship cannot be recast as consent obtained by misrepresentation; proceedings quashed

cases.name: State of Karnataka v. Sadiq Pasha
cases.bench: JB Pardiwala, K Vinod Chandran JJ
cases.tag: NDPS case not quashed at threshold just because it rests on co-accused disclosures, though they alone cannot convict

cases.name: Gopal Pathak v. Nitin alias Pappu
cases.tag: Courts may compare disputed signatures themselves; expert opinion is needed only in doubtful cases

cases.name: Kasif Sahabuddin Khan v. State of Maharashtra
cases.tag: The bar on anticipatory bail in s.482(4) BNSS is not absolute; court can check if the offence is prima facie made out

cases.name: Krushna Arun Shingare v. State of Maharashtra
cases.tag: Boilerplate grounds of arrest without a factual link to the offence do not comply; DGP told to revise arrest forms

cases.name: Bhimaji Parshuram Sabale v. Union of India
cases.tag: Informing an NDPS undertrial through the jail about extending investigation time is not producing him before court

cases.name: Vijay v. State of Maharashtra
cases.tag: Pouring kerosene on the wife and telling her to die is active instigation under s.306 IPC

cases.name: M. Prema v. State of Tamil Nadu
cases.tag: Unless recruitment rules say otherwise, ad hoc, temporary or compassionate appointees count seniority from regularisation; earlier stop-gap service cannot place them above direct recruits.

cases.name: Ramkrushna Prahlad Dongardive v. State of Maharashtra
cases.bench: Ujjal Bhuyan, Atul S. Chandurkar JJ
cases.tag: Accused's failure to explain a seizure is not incriminating; prosecution must prove a valid seizure

cases.name: Modern Asset v. KNK Constructions Pvt. Ltd.
cases.bench: J.B. Pardiwala, K. Vinod Chandran JJ
cases.topic: Clean slate – set-off in post-CIRP arbitration
cases.tag: An operational creditor's claim extinguished under S. 31 IBC cannot yield any recovery, but may be pleaded as set-off, up to its full amount, against the resolution applicant's arbitral claim for pre-CIRP dues.

cases.name: MEPCO Industries Ltd. v. Commissioner of Income Tax
cases.bench: Prashant Kumar Mishra, Shree Chandrashekhar JJ
cases.tag: Electricity subsidy meant to reduce running costs is a taxable revenue receipt under the purpose test

cases.name: V. Pon. Paneerselvam v. S. Regupathy
cases.bench: Prashant Kumar Mishra, Shree Chandrashekhar JJ
cases.tag: An election petition must be presented by the petitioner personally; one filed through counsel was rightly dismissed

cases.name: Appa v. State of Maharashtra
cases.bench: Prashant Kumar Mishra, Shree Chandrashekhar JJ
cases.tag: No conviction for causing hurt in robbery (s.394 IPC) unless robbery or attempted robbery is proved

cases.name: Bharatbhai Hirjibhai Shankar v. State of Gujarat
cases.tag: Selling garments with religious images is not an offence under s.295A IPC without deliberate, malicious intent

cases.name: M/s JPEE Drugs v. State of Madhya Pradesh
cases.bench: Vikram Nath, Augustine George Masih, Sandeep Mehta JJ
cases.tag: If the State's own delay or failure to draw a second sample robs a supplier of a real chance to retest a drug batch, blacklisting or debarment resting on the disputed test report cannot stand.

cases.name: Ajit Kumar v. State of Jharkhand
cases.bench: Ujjal Bhuyan, Atul S. Chandurkar JJ
cases.tag: No conviction under the Prevention of Corruption Act without proof of both demand and acceptance of a bribe

cases.name: Union of India v. Hariom Projects Pvt. Ltd.
cases.tag: A tribunal under s.17 cannot hear an appeal against a court's s.9 order; a High Court cannot delegate a s.37 appeal to it

cases.name: Geeta Bai v. K. Arjun Singh
cases.tag: A compromise decree passed without a necessary party is a nullity; that party can seek recall from the same court

cases.name: Umar v. State of Uttar Pradesh
cases.bench: JB Pardiwala, K Vinod Chandran JJ
cases.tag: Where cognizance is taken after BNSS came into force, the accused must first be heard under the s.223 proviso

cases.name: Kanha @ Kanhaiya Singh v. State of Madhya Pradesh
cases.tag: Judges must not apply personal views of morality when deciding bail

cases.name: Santosh Gurung v. State of Sikkim
cases.tag: A conviction cannot rest only on the accused's s.313 statement to fill gaps in the prosecution case

cases.name: Sainaba v. State of Kerala
cases.tag: A demand notice sent by registered post to the correct address is served even if a family member receives it

cases.name: Orris Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. v. Rakesh Kumar Gupta
cases.tag: NCLT can recall admission of a fraudulently filed s.9 IBC application but must decide separately if CIRP continues

cases.name: Shikha Ghosh v. Axis Bank Ltd.
cases.tag: An award by an arbitrator appointed unilaterally by the bank is void and unenforceable against the borrower

cases.name: Bombay Garage Ahmedabad Ltd. v. J P Iscon Pvt. Ltd.
cases.tag: Omitting specific performance without leave under Order 2 Rule 2 bars a later suit for it, even after withdrawal under Order 23

cases.name: Mulla Afroz v. Union of India
cases.tag: A custodial confession without independent material cannot justify preventive detention; NSA order quashed with costs

cases.name: Seema Sharma v. State of Punjab
cases.bench: Surya Kant CJI, Joymalya Bagchi, V. Mohana JJ
cases.tag: Where an inquiry found candidates were assaulted and nominations obstructed, polls in those 50 Punjab wards were set aside and re-run under a High Court monitoring committee; order not to be a precedent.

cases.name: XXX v. State of Kerala
cases.tag: Neither parents nor police can make an adult woman return to her parental home against her will; police may still complete a missing-person inquiry.

cases.name: Tulk v. Moxhay
cases.tag: Negative covenants bind purchasers with notice

cases.name: Hadley v. Baxendale
cases.tag: Damages limited to losses arising naturally or in the parties' contemplation

cases.name: Rylands v. Fletcher
cases.tag: Liability for escape of dangerous things from non-natural use of land

cases.name: Chinnaya v. Ramayya
cases.tag: Consideration may move from a third party

cases.name: Carlill v. Carbolic Smoke Ball Co
cases.tag: A general offer can be accepted by performing its conditions

cases.name: Harvey v. Facey
cases.tag: Stating a lowest price is information, not an offer

cases.name: Salomon v. A. Salomon & Co
cases.tag: A company is a separate legal person from its members

cases.name: Mohori Bibee v. Dharmodas Ghose
cases.tag: A minor's agreement is void ab initio

notes.facts: Dharmodas Ghose, a minor, mortgaged his property to moneylender Brahmo Dutt for Rs 20,000. The lender's agent knew he was a minor. Dharmodas (through his mother) sued to set the mortgage aside; the lender's estate sought repayment of money advanced.
issues: Is a minor's contract void or voidable?
Must the minor return the money received?
Is the minor estopped by his misrepresentation of age?
notes.held: A minor's agreement is void from the start under ss.10 and 11 of the Indian Contract Act. Sections 64 and 65 do not apply because there was never a contract, so no refund was ordered. Estoppel did not apply because the lender's agent knew the truth.
notes.ratio: An agreement with a minor is void ab initio, and the minor cannot be compelled to return benefits under ss.64–65 of the Contract Act.
notes.matters: The starting point for capacity in Indian contract law. Contrast s.33 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963, which now lets courts order restitution in some cases.
notes.history: Estoppel rule then in s.115 Indian Evidence Act, now s.121 Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023.

cases.name: Lalman Shukla v. Gauri Dutt
cases.tag: No acceptance without knowledge of the offer

notes.facts: Gauri Dutt's nephew went missing. He sent his servant Lalman to search. After Lalman left, Gauri Dutt announced a reward of Rs 501. Lalman found the boy without knowing of the reward, then claimed it.
issues: Can a person accept an offer they do not know about?
notes.held: No contract was formed. Acceptance requires knowledge of the offer, so Lalman's claim failed.
notes.ratio: There can be no acceptance of an offer, and so no contract, without knowledge of the offer.
notes.matters: Standard comparison with Carlill v. Carbolic Smoke Ball Co. on general offers.
notes.history: Still cited for s.2(b) Indian Contract Act.

cases.name: Abdul Aziz v. Masum Ali
cases.tag: Promise to subscribe to a mosque fund unenforceable without detriment

cases.name: Barendra Kumar Ghosh v. Emperor
cases.tag: Those who also serve who stand and wait: common intention liability

cases.name: Donoghue v. Stevenson
cases.tag: Neighbour principle: duty to those closely and directly affected

cases.name: Pakala Narayana Swami v. Emperor
cases.tag: Statements about circumstances of death are relevant as dying declarations

cases.name: Mahboob Shah v. Emperor
cases.tag: Common intention needs a prearranged plan, which may form on the spot

cases.name: Pulukuri Kottaya v. Emperor
cases.tag: Only the part of a statement that distinctly leads to discovery is admissible

cases.name: Associated Provincial Picture Houses v. Wednesbury Corporation
cases.tag: Wednesbury unreasonableness: a decision no reasonable authority could reach

cases.name: A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras
cases.tag: Fundamental rights read as separate codes; narrow reading of 'procedure established by law' (later overruled)

notes.facts: Communist leader A.K. Gopalan was detained under the Preventive Detention Act, 1950. He argued the detention violated Articles 19, 21 and 22.
issues: Does 'procedure established by law' include principles of natural justice or due process?
Must a law under Article 21 also satisfy Article 19?
notes.held: The majority held that each Fundamental Right is a self-contained code. 'Law' in Article 21 means law enacted by the State; the court refused to read in American due process. Only s.14 of the Act, which barred disclosure of the grounds of detention to the court, was struck down.
notes.ratio: Articles 19 and 21 operate in separate fields; a law satisfying Article 21 need not be tested against Article 19.
notes.matters: Read it as the starting point that later cases reversed. Fazl Ali J's dissent is the view the court eventually adopted.
notes.history: Mutual-exclusivity view overruled by R.C. Cooper v. Union of India (1970); narrow reading of Article 21 rejected in Maneka Gandhi (1978).

cases.name: Romesh Thappar v. State of Madras
cases.tag: Freedom of speech includes freedom of circulation; ban on a journal struck down

cases.name: State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan
cases.tag: Communal G.O. on college admissions struck down; led to the First Amendment adding Article 15(4)

cases.name: Shankari Prasad v. Union of India
cases.tag: Parliament can amend fundamental rights; 'law' in Article 13 excludes constitutional amendments

cases.name: State of West Bengal v. Anwar Ali Sarkar
cases.tag: Reasonable classification test: intelligible differentia with a rational nexus to the object

cases.name: Satyabrata Ghose v. Mugneeram Bangur
cases.tag: Section 56 covers impracticability, but temporary requisition did not frustrate

notes.facts: Mugneeram Bangur & Co. sold plots in a Calcutta development and promised to build roads and drains. During the Second World War, part of the land was requisitioned by the government. The company told the buyer to take a refund or complete later.
issues: Was the contract frustrated by the requisition?
What does 'impossible' mean in s.56 of the Contract Act?
notes.held: 'Impossible' in s.56 is not limited to physical impossibility; it covers performance that becomes impracticable and useless for the object the parties had in view. But here the requisition was temporary and no time limit was essential, so the contract was not frustrated.
notes.ratio: Section 56 is exhaustive in India; impossibility includes impracticability that destroys the foundation of the contract, but mere delay or hardship is not enough.
notes.matters: The leading Indian case on frustration; English cases are only a guide.
notes.history: Followed in Naihati Jute Mills (1968) and Energy Watchdog v. CERC (2017).

cases.name: K.M. Nanavati v. State of Maharashtra
cases.tag: Grave and sudden provocation; cooling time defeats the exception

notes.facts: Naval Commander Nanavati's wife told him of her affair with Prem Ahuja. He dropped his family at a cinema, collected a revolver from his ship, went to Ahuja's flat and shot him. A jury acquitted him 8:1; the judge referred the case to the High Court, which convicted him of murder.
issues: Was the killing covered by Exception 1 to s.300 IPC (grave and sudden provocation)?
Could the High Court interfere with the jury verdict?
notes.held: The conviction for murder was upheld. The test is whether a reasonable person of the same class of society, in the accused's situation, would be so provoked as to lose self-control. About three hours had passed, giving time to cool down, so the provocation was neither sudden nor operative.
notes.ratio: Provocation must be both grave and sudden, and the accused must have acted while deprived of self-control; time to cool down defeats the exception.
notes.matters: Still the core test for provocation. The case is also linked with the end of jury trials in India.
notes.history: s.300 Exception 1 IPC is now Exception 1 to s.101, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.

cases.name: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
cases.tag: Parliament can amend any part of the Constitution but not its basic structure

notes.facts: Swami Kesavananda Bharati, head of the Edneer Mutt in Kasaragod, challenged Kerala land reform laws that restricted how the mutt could manage its property. The challenge grew into a review of the 24th, 25th and 29th Constitutional Amendments and of Parliament's power to amend Fundamental Rights.
issues: Is Parliament's power to amend the Constitution under Article 368 unlimited?
Can Fundamental Rights be amended or taken away?
Was Golak Nath v. State of Punjab (1967) correctly decided?
notes.held: Parliament can amend any part of the Constitution, including Fundamental Rights, but it cannot alter or destroy its basic structure. Golak Nath was overruled. The 24th Amendment was upheld; the part of Article 31C that excluded judicial review was struck down.
notes.ratio: The power to amend under Article 368 does not include the power to destroy the Constitution's basic structure or framework.
notes.matters: Every constitutional amendment since 1973 is tested against this doctrine. The judges did not give a closed list, so the content of 'basic structure' has grown case by case (judicial review, federalism, secularism, free and fair elections).
notes.history: Applied in Indira Gandhi v. Raj Narain (1975), Minerva Mills (1980), I.R. Coelho (2007) and the NJAC case (2016).

cases.name: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
cases.tag: Procedure under Article 21 must be just, fair and reasonable; Articles 14, 19 and 21 read together

notes.facts: Maneka Gandhi's passport was impounded under s.10(3)(c) of the Passports Act, 1967 'in the interests of the general public'. The government refused to give reasons and she was given no hearing.
issues: Does 'procedure established by law' in Article 21 mean any procedure enacted by the legislature?
Are Articles 14, 19 and 21 separate, mutually exclusive codes?
Is the right to travel abroad part of personal liberty?
notes.held: A law depriving a person of personal liberty must prescribe a procedure that is just, fair and reasonable, not arbitrary or oppressive. Articles 14, 19 and 21 must be read together. Natural justice (audi alteram partem) is read into the Passports Act. The right to go abroad is part of personal liberty.
notes.ratio: Any procedure under Article 21 must satisfy the test of reasonableness under Articles 14 and 19; Articles 14, 19 and 21 form an interlinked 'golden triangle'.
notes.matters: It turned Article 21 into the source of a long list of unenumerated rights (speedy trial, legal aid, livelihood, privacy) and brought something close to due process into Indian law.
notes.history: Departs from A.K. Gopalan (1950). Foundation for Puttaswamy (2017).

cases.tag: Speedy trial is part of Article 21; release of undertrials detained too long

cases.name: Dhanpal Chettiar v. Yesodai Ammal
cases.tag: No notice under s.106 TPA needed for eviction under rent control laws

cases.name: Minerva Mills v. Union of India
cases.tag: Limited amending power and the balance between Parts III and IV are basic features

notes.facts: Minerva Mills, a Bangalore textile mill, was taken over under the Sick Textile Undertakings (Nationalisation) Act, 1974. The owners challenged ss.4 and 55 of the 42nd Amendment.
issues: Could Parliament exclude judicial review of amendments (Article 368(4), (5))?
Could Article 31C protect laws implementing any Directive Principle from Articles 14 and 19?
notes.held: Section 55 of the 42nd Amendment was struck down because limited amending power is itself part of the basic structure. Section 4 was struck down because the balance between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles is a basic feature.
notes.ratio: Parliament cannot convert its limited amending power into an unlimited one, and the harmony between Parts III and IV is part of the basic structure.
notes.matters: Confirms and extends Kesavananda; often quoted on the 'golden triangle' of Articles 14, 19 and 21.
notes.history: Followed in Waman Rao (1981) and I.R. Coelho (2007).

cases.name: Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab
cases.tag: Death penalty only in the rarest of rare cases

notes.facts: Bachan Singh was sentenced to death for murder. The case raised the constitutional validity of the death penalty under s.302 IPC and the sentencing procedure in s.354(3) CrPC.
issues: Is the death penalty for murder constitutional?
How should courts choose between life imprisonment and death?
notes.held: The death penalty is constitutional, but life imprisonment is the rule and death the exception, to be imposed only in the 'rarest of rare' cases when the alternative is unquestionably foreclosed. Courts must weigh aggravating and mitigating circumstances of both the crime and the criminal. Bhagwati J dissented.
notes.ratio: Death may be imposed only in the rarest of rare cases, after balancing aggravating and mitigating circumstances relating to both crime and offender.
notes.matters: Governs all capital sentencing. Applied through Machhi Singh (1983) and more recently Manoj v. State of MP (2022) on mitigation investigation.
notes.history: Murder punishment now under s.103, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.

cases.name: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (Oleum Gas Leak)
cases.tag: Absolute liability for hazardous industries

notes.facts: In December 1985, oleum gas leaked from Shriram Food and Fertiliser Industries in Delhi, affecting many people. M.C. Mehta's pending PIL raised the liability of such enterprises.
issues: What is the liability of an enterprise carrying on a hazardous or inherently dangerous activity?
Should the exceptions in Rylands v. Fletcher apply?
notes.held: An enterprise engaged in a hazardous or inherently dangerous activity is absolutely liable for harm caused by an accident, with none of the exceptions available under strict liability. Compensation must be related to the size and capacity of the enterprise so it has a deterrent effect.
notes.ratio: Hazardous enterprises owe an absolute, non-delegable duty to the community, and are liable without the Rylands v. Fletcher exceptions.
notes.matters: India's own tort rule, developed after Bhopal; reflected in the Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991.
notes.history: Reaffirmed in Indian Council for Enviro-Legal Action (1996).

cases.name: Indra Sawhney v. Union of India
cases.tag: 27% OBC quota upheld; creamy layer excluded; 50% ceiling; no reservation in promotions

notes.facts: Challenge to the 1990 office memorandum implementing the Mandal Commission (27% reservation for OBCs) and the 1991 memorandum adding 10% for economically backward sections among other classes.
issues: Is 27% OBC reservation valid?
Can backwardness be identified by caste?
Is there a ceiling on reservations?
Are reservations allowed in promotions?
notes.held: 27% OBC reservation was upheld; caste can be a basis for identifying backward classes. The creamy layer must be excluded. Reservations should ordinarily not exceed 50%. No reservation in promotions (applied prospectively). The 10% reservation on purely economic grounds was struck down.
notes.ratio: Reservations under Article 16(4) must exclude the creamy layer, should not ordinarily exceed 50%, and do not extend to promotions.
notes.matters: The base case for all reservation questions.
notes.history: Promotions: 77th Amendment added Article 16(4A). Economic criterion: 103rd Amendment (EWS) upheld in Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India (2022).

cases.name: S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
cases.tag: Article 356 proclamations are judicially reviewable; floor test; secularism is basic structure

notes.facts: The Karnataka government of S.R. Bommai was dismissed under Article 356 in 1989 without a floor test. Dismissals in other states were heard together.
issues: Is a proclamation under Article 356 open to judicial review?
How should a government's majority be tested?
notes.held: A proclamation under Article 356 is subject to judicial review on grounds of mala fides or irrelevant material. Majority must be tested on the floor of the House. The Assembly should not be dissolved before Parliament approves the proclamation. Secularism is part of the basic structure.
notes.ratio: The President's satisfaction under Article 356 is justiciable, and the floor of the House is the proper place to test majority.
notes.matters: Sharply reduced misuse of Article 356 and is the key federalism case.
notes.history: Applied in Rameshwar Prasad (2006) and Nabam Rebia (2016).

cases.name: D.K. Basu v. State of West Bengal
cases.tag: Arrest and custody safeguards; compensation for custodial violence

notes.facts: D.K. Basu, chairman of Legal Aid Services, West Bengal, wrote to the Chief Justice about deaths in police custody. The letter was treated as a writ petition.
issues: What safeguards must accompany arrest and detention?
Is the State liable to pay compensation for custodial violence?
notes.held: The court laid down requirements including identification tags for arresting officers, an arrest memo attested by a witness and countersigned by the arrestee, informing a friend or relative, medical examination every 48 hours, and access to a lawyer during interrogation. Violation attracts departmental action and contempt; compensation is available in public law for custodial violence.
notes.ratio: Custodial violence violates Article 21, and arrest must follow minimum procedural safeguards; the State is liable in public law for such violations.
notes.matters: The standard checklist for lawful arrest and the basis for compensation claims in custodial death cases.
notes.history: Largely codified in ss.41B–41D CrPC (2009), now ss.36–38, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.

cases.name: Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan
cases.tag: Guidelines against workplace sexual harassment, drawing on CEDAW

notes.facts: Bhanwari Devi, a social worker (saathin) in a Rajasthan government programme, was gang-raped in 1992 after she tried to stop a child marriage. Women's groups, including Vishaka, filed a PIL.
issues: Does sexual harassment at the workplace violate Fundamental Rights?
Can the court lay down binding norms where there is no law?
notes.held: Sexual harassment at work violates Articles 14, 15, 19(1)(g) and 21. Where domestic law is silent, international conventions such as CEDAW can be read into Fundamental Rights if consistent with them. The court framed the Vishaka Guidelines, binding until Parliament legislated.
notes.ratio: In the absence of domestic law, international conventions consistent with Fundamental Rights may be read into them, and the court may issue binding guidelines under Article 32.
notes.matters: A leading example of judicial law-making to fill a legislative gap and of using international law in rights cases.
notes.history: Replaced by the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 (POSH Act).

cases.name: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar
cases.tag: No routine arrest for offences up to 7 years; s.41/41A checklist (now s.35 BNSS)

notes.facts: The petitioner, accused by his wife under s.498A IPC and s.4 Dowry Prohibition Act, sought anticipatory bail fearing arrest.
issues: When may police arrest without warrant for offences punishable up to seven years?
What must a magistrate check before authorising detention?
notes.held: Police must not arrest automatically. They must be satisfied that arrest is necessary under the s.41(1)(b) CrPC criteria and record reasons using a checklist. Where arrest is not needed, a notice of appearance under s.41A must be served within two weeks. Magistrates must scrutinise the reasons before authorising detention. Non-compliance invites departmental action and contempt.
notes.ratio: Arrest for offences punishable up to seven years requires recorded necessity under s.41 CrPC, and magistrates must not authorise detention mechanically.
notes.matters: Central to arrest and remand practice; extended to all such offences in Satender Kumar Antil v. CBI (2022).

cases.name: Justice K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India
cases.tag: Privacy is a fundamental right under Article 21 and Part III

notes.facts: Retired High Court judge K.S. Puttaswamy challenged the Aadhaar scheme. The government argued there was no Fundamental Right to privacy, relying on M.P. Sharma (1954, 8 judges) and Kharak Singh (1962, 6 judges). The question was referred to a 9-judge bench.
issues: Is the right to privacy a Fundamental Right under the Constitution?
Were M.P. Sharma and Kharak Singh correctly decided on this point?
notes.held: Privacy is intrinsic to life and personal liberty under Article 21 and to the freedoms in Part III. M.P. Sharma and Kharak Singh were overruled to the extent they held otherwise. The plurality also said ADM Jabalpur (1976) was wrongly decided.
notes.ratio: The right to privacy is protected as an intrinsic part of Article 21 and Part III; any intrusion must satisfy legality, a legitimate aim and proportionality.
notes.matters: It set the three-part test (legality, need, proportionality) now used for surveillance, data protection and bodily-autonomy cases, and was relied on in Navtej Singh Johar and Joseph Shine.
notes.history: Aadhaar itself was decided separately in Puttaswamy (Aadhaar) (2019) 1 SCC 1.

cases.name: Shayara Bano v. Union of India
cases.tag: Instant triple talaq set aside

notes.facts: Shayara Bano was divorced by her husband through talaq-e-biddat (instant, irrevocable triple talaq). She challenged the practice.
issues: Is talaq-e-biddat valid?
Is it protected as an essential religious practice?
notes.held: By majority, talaq-e-biddat was set aside. Nariman and Lalit JJ held it manifestly arbitrary under Article 14, so s.2 of the Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act, 1937 was void to that extent. Kurian Joseph J held it was not part of the Quran's teaching. Khehar CJ and Nazeer J dissented and suggested Parliament legislate.
notes.ratio: Instant triple talaq is not legally valid; the majority reasoning differs, with the plurality applying 'manifest arbitrariness' under Article 14.
notes.matters: Note the split reasoning: there is no single majority ratio on manifest arbitrariness, but the doctrine was later used in Joseph Shine.
notes.history: Followed by the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019.

cases.name: Independent Thought v. Union of India

cases.name: Innoventive Industries Ltd. v. ICICI Bank
cases.tag: First major IBC ruling: once the NCLT finds a financial debt in default it must admit a complete S. 7 application, a dispute does not stop it, and the IBC prevails over the Maharashtra relief undertakings law.

cases.name: Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India
cases.tag: Section 377 IPC read down; consensual adult same-sex relations decriminalised

notes.facts: Dancer Navtej Singh Johar and others challenged s.377 IPC, which criminalised 'carnal intercourse against the order of nature', after Suresh Kumar Koushal (2013) had restored it.
issues: Does s.377, as applied to consensual sex between adults, violate Articles 14, 15, 19 and 21?
notes.held: Section 377 is unconstitutional to the extent it criminalises consensual sexual conduct between adults. It survives for non-consensual acts and bestiality. Suresh Kumar Koushal was overruled.
notes.ratio: Criminalising consensual sexual conduct between adults based on sexual orientation violates dignity, privacy, equality and expression; constitutional morality prevails over social morality.
notes.matters: Key authority on constitutional morality and transformative constitutionalism.
notes.history: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 has no provision equivalent to s.377 IPC.

cases.name: Joseph Shine v. Union of India
cases.tag: Adultery (s.497 IPC) struck down

notes.facts: Joseph Shine challenged s.497 IPC, which punished only a man for sex with another man's wife without the husband's consent, and s.198(2) CrPC, which let only the husband complain.
issues: Does s.497 violate Articles 14, 15 and 21?
notes.held: Section 497 and s.198(2) CrPC (as applied to it) are unconstitutional. The provision treated a woman as her husband's property and was arbitrary. Sowmithri Vishnu (1985) and V. Revathi (1988) were overruled. Adultery remains a civil ground for divorce.
notes.ratio: A penal provision built on the idea of a wife as her husband's property violates equality, non-discrimination and dignity.
notes.matters: Applies Puttaswamy's dignity and autonomy reasoning to criminal law.
notes.history: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 does not contain an adultery offence.
